title: the water before the words
hookLine: washing before prayer: why these parts, in this order

lines: A ROW OF TAPS BY THE DOOR.
cards: Near the door of many mosques there's a row of taps along a wall, a low ledge to sit on, a drain along the floor. Before the prayer, people stop here first. Sleeves up, shoes off.
Water over the hands, into the mouth, over the face, up the arms, over the feet. If you grew up with it, you could do it with your eyes closed. So: why these parts, and why this order?

teach.h: WUDU — FROM A ROOT OF BRIGHTNESS.
teach.b: It's called wudu, from a root with the sense of brightness, the way a washed face shines.
The core is one verse of the Qur'an: “When ye rise up for prayer, wash your faces, and your hands up to the elbows,” then wipe the head, and then the feet.

Face, arms, head, feet: that's the order, and it comes from the verse itself. The rest, the hands first, the mouth and nose, the ears, families learned from the way the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ showed his companions.
Here's the surprising part. It isn't really about dirt. People make wudu when they're already clean.

teach.h: THE WRONGS RUN OFF WITH THE WATER.
teach.b: A saying of the Prophet pictures it this way: as the water runs off your face, the wrongs your eyes looked at run off with it; off the hands, what the hands did; off the feet, where the feet went.
So it's a reset, done with the body: the step between the street and the prayer. It lasts until something breaks it, like sleep, so it isn't always a fresh wash for every prayer.
And when there's no water, or water would harm you, the same verse allows clean earth instead. That's called tayammum. The reset is never out of reach.

how: Muslims make wudu before prayer unless they are still in a state of wudu from an earlier washing; mosques have washing areas with taps, and at home it's done at an ordinary sink.

games.q: what's inside the washing — tap the pairs.
p: clean earth, when there's no water

s: wudu is described in the Qur'an itself
one verse sets out the core: face, arms to the elbows, head and feet (5:6).
you have to make a fresh wudu before every single prayer
it lasts until something breaks it, like sleep. many renew it anyway, for the fresh start.
without water, there's no way to prepare for prayer
the same verse allows tayammum: touching clean earth and wiping the face and hands.

games.q: you're in a desert, the prayer time has come, and there's no water anywhere. what does the verse allow?
o: skip the prayer until you find water.
use clean earth to wipe the face and hands.
games.why: tayammum: clean earth stands in for water. the reset is never out of reach.

games.q: put the washing in the Qur'an's order.

practice: Three breaths with the bell. If there's water near you, wash your hands slowly and feel it run off your fingers. If not, rest your hands open and picture cool water over them, then over your face.
With each breath out, let one thing from today run off with it.

wordCard.voice: Wudu. The washing before prayer: face, arms, head and feet. A reset with water. Third word.

orig.note: Arabic: the washing before prayer, from a root of brightness and cleanness.

carryVoice: Your line: rinse the day off. The day doesn't have to come with you into the prayer. Day three.
